testId: testim-migrated/tests/webstore/login/verify-sign-in-and-registration-labels.spec.ts > Webstore - Login > the registration page carries its headings, field labels and controls

scenario.summary: Guest opens /signup and checks the three headings, the username, e-mail, password and confirm-password labels and the Create Account, Cancel and Login Now controls, then clicks Login Now and checks the sign-in form. Read-only, no account is created.
steps: Check the Create An Account, Register for an account and Already have an account? headings
Check the username, e-mail address, password and confirm-password labels
Check the Create Account, Cancel and Login Now button texts
Click Login Now; check the username input is visible and the Sign In heading
stateChanges: None (guest, read-only; the registration form is never submitted)
assertions: createAccountHeading, registerForAccountHeading, alreadyHaveAccountHeading contain signUp.heading / registerForAccountHeading / alreadyHaveAccountHeading
createUsernameLabel, createEmailAddressLabel, passwordLabel, createConfirmPasswordLabel contain the signUp labels
createAccountSubmitButton, signupCancelButton, loginNowButton contain the signUp button texts
After Login Now: usernameInput visible, signInHeading contains signIn.heading
evidence: Title and step labels match the flow; linked cases ZPD-TC-9152..9155 (scan, shared by the describe)

UI text only: every value is a heading, field label or button text asserted with toContainText -> expected-output; '/signup' is the start URL (config). No record of the environment is read, so no need

Masked labels, not credentials: source 4 (signUp.usernameLabel), source 5 (signUp.emailAddressLabel), source 6 (signUp.passwordLabel) and source 7 (signUp.confirmPasswordLabel) are masked only because the key contains 'username'/'email'/'password'; the spec asserts them with toContainText on the sign-up field labels (lblUserName, lblEmail, lblPassword, lblConfirmPassword) and never types them -> expected-output. Values stay masked
Store: no test.use baseURL; the spec runs on the project's default webstore baseURL (the same webstore as the other login specs). It reads no record, so no store param is needed
